assessment.rationale: Read from the full text, not the abstract, which is why content_depth is fulltext_snapshot. Directness direct: the paper derives and tests this distinction explicitly. Scope close rather than exact: derived at 0.12B-2B under industrial token budgets, while we run 50.33M under 300 charged seconds, and the Hessian-sharpness argument is asymptotic in a way 600 steps may not reach. The immediate value is diagnostic -- it says our staged arm is misconfigured -- which is a cheap correction regardless of whether the magnitude transfers.

metrics.name: weight_decay_prescription
metrics.result: A per-layer rule, not a global one. Our two candidate scale vectors sit on norms feeding c_q/c_k/c_v and c_fc, so both are Input-Norm and both should carry weight decay; the staged arm sets weight_decay=0.0, contrary to this.

locators.excerpt: Input-Norm layers are 'the RMSNorm layer immediately followed by a linear transformation'... Output-Norm layers are 'the RMSNorm layer not immediately followed by a linear transformation', including Q/K-Norm and attention/FFN output normalization. For Input-Norm, weight decay keeps the parameterization balanced and 'controls Hessian sharpness', preventing divergence of lambda_max of the loss Hessian. For Output-Norm, weight decay would 'undesirably restrict expressivity'.
locators.location: full text, Individual Weight Decay (IWD) section

scope.budget: industrial-scale token budgets; no wall-clock constraint
scope.model: dense and MoE decoder LLMs, 0.12B-2B, Pre-Norm with RMSNorm scale vectors

statement: Weight decay applied to a normalization scale vector is beneficial when the norm is immediately followed by a linear transformation (Input-Norm) and harmful when it is not (Output-Norm), because the former controls Hessian sharpness while the latter directly parameterizes a submodule's output and so constrains expressivity.
